rules.statement: When code uses a regex or pattern to drop or keep lines, give its tests a case for every form the pattern is meant to match and at least one near-miss it must not match, and assert which lines remain.
rules.why: Otherwise a later edit to the pattern could drop a rule that should be kept, or keep one that should be dropped, and no test would fail.
rules.check: Look for a new or changed filtering pattern whose tests skip some of the variants it targets (for example, the bare form) or have no near-miss case that must stay unmatched.

rules.statement: When the same pattern or logic has to be copied into two files because one ships standalone and can't load a shared helper, add a test that reads or runs both copies and fails when they differ, rather than relying on a 'change both together' comment.
rules.why: If one copy changes without the other, the two code paths will quietly disagree, and a comment alone does nothing to stop that.
rules.check: Look for duplicated patterns or logic marked with a 'keep in sync' or 'change both together' comment, and check whether a test compares the copies.
